about.description: A desktop application for managing Kubernetes clusters with a visual interface. Built with Go, Wails and React.

welcome.title: Welcome to Kube Inspector
welcome.content: This quick tour will show you the key features of the app. Use the arrow buttons to navigate between steps, or press Skip to exit at any time.

cluster.title: Cluster Configuration
cluster.content: Select or switch between your Kubernetes clusters here. Use the + button to add a new cluster, the pencil to edit the active one, and the graph icon to view the resource graph.

sidebar.title: Resource Explorer
sidebar.content: Browse all Kubernetes resources from the sidebar. Resources are grouped into Workloads, Networking, Config & Security, Storage, and Cluster categories. Click any item to open it as a panel.

workspace.title: Main Workspace
workspace.content: Resource panels open here. You can drag tabs to rearrange them, split the workspace horizontally or vertically, and resize panels by dragging the dividers between them.

yaml.title: YAML Editor
yaml.content: Apply raw YAML directly to your cluster. Paste or write Kubernetes manifests and click Apply. Supports multi-document YAML files (separated by ---).

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.content: Open an interactive terminal session. Run kubectl commands, inspect resources, and interact with your cluster directly from within the app.

done.title: You're all set!
done.content: You now know the essentials of Kube Inspector. Double-click any row in a resource list to view its YAML, and use the log button on workload rows to stream live logs.

diagnostics.exportNote: A zip containing this report, the health-check results and the log files below. Home directory paths, cluster names, bearer tokens and API server addresses are removed first. Nothing is sent anywhere — the file is written where you choose and it is yours to share or not.
diagnostics.retentionNote: Log files older than 7 days are deleted automatically.
diagnostics.checksNone: No checks have been run yet.
diagnostics.logLevelHint: Applies to this window's backend. Other windows of this app share it; a separately launched instance does not, until it restarts.
diagnostics.noMatch: Nothing matches. The log only holds today's records.

node.shellTooltip: Open a root shell on this node
node.shellWarning: This creates a <1>privileged pod</1> on the node and gives you <1>root access to the host</1> — inside the node’s own process, network and mount namespaces.
node.shellCleanup: Kubernetes has no node-exec API, so the shell is reached through a helper pod. It is deleted as soon as you close the terminal tab.

node.drainWarning: This will first <1>cordon</1> the node (mark it unschedulable), then evict all pods except DaemonSet and mirror pods.
